subject: Memory Allocation issue with STAN running in Google Cloud?

messages.author: e1c430550f86b1f6
messages.subject: Memory Allocation issue with STAN running in Google Cloud?
parts:
hi guys,

I tired running a bunch of STAN scripts (as part of my program) in a Google Cloud vm via rstan. When I enabled mc.cores = 2 (my "trail" VM can only have 2 cores max), my R script would get stuck and when I press Ctrl-C, I can see R is complaining "memory allocation problem". Thought such problem does not seem to have arise when I run with mc.cores=1.

Anyone might have insight?

The Google VM is running Debian Jessie and R 3.2.1 (from CRAN).

From top, i can still circa 1G of free memory

Cheers,
Andy

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Memory Allocation issue with STAN running in Google Cloud?
parts:
RStan allocates memory to store the draws ahead of time. You
can either try running CmdStan, which streams out the output,
or you can try running fewer draws, thinning more, or saving fewer
parameters. If there's no problem with mc.cores=1 then you are
probably just exhausting memory when you try two. Two runs should
use twice as much memory --- there's no sharing (yet, anyway).

- Bob
